newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks close with heavy losses after Dow drop.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks close with heavy losses after Dow drop.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks slid to a sharply lower close on Friday after a drop on Wall Street overnight left investors jittery going into the weekend.

"People are worried that they might see another correction tonight in the Dow. It has run up quite a lot in the last two or three weeks," said Henry Lui, research analyst at Mansion House Research. He said investors were taking cover just in case.
The Hang Seng Index dropped 230.78 points, or 1.7 percent, to 13,379.55. Turnover was HK$11.12 billion compared with HK$8.28 billion on Thursday.
The Dow industrials tumbled 94.28 points, or 1.38 percent, to 6,755.75 on Thursday on the largest trading volume ever.

"Overnight there were sell programmes in the U.S. which depressed the Dow Jones towards the end of the session. It was probably similar in Hong Kong with some sell programmes," said Peter So, deputy head of research at Schroder Securities.

"The market is oversold because fundamentally earnings are improving. Banks are getting more business while the property market is still performing very well. I think it is just some profit-taking because the market has gone up so much," he said.
So said this week's market tone had dampened sentiment, prompting some investors to stay on the sidelines. The blue-chip index fell 476.85 points, or 3.44 percent, over the week.
"The futures market has been very weak and has led the decline," So said.
January Hang Seng Index futures dropped 320 points to 13,265 on Friday.

The commercial and industrial sector led the market's decline, with Hutchison Whampoa shares taking a beating and ending down HK$2.75 at HK$61.25. The share had been up four percent this week as of Thursday's close.
Wharf Holdings dropped HK$1.20 to HK$36.60 and Swire Pacific shed HK$2.00 to HK$73.75.

Hongkong Electric fell HK$0.20 to HK$26.80. Brokers said an announcement by an independent board committee of the company saying Hutchison's HK$26.50 per share general offer undervalued the utility had brought some support to the stock.
Mansion House's Lui said the Hang Seng Index should find some support around current levels and a steady Wall Street should tempt investors back into the market.
